rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING THE TAMPERING OF VOTES AS A HEINOUS CRIME AND PROVIDING PENALTY THEREOF BY AMENDING FURTHER SECTION 261 (bb) (2) AND ALSO SECTION 264 OF BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 881
rows.abstract: Rationale: Fraudulent activities during elections are very rampant in our society ... More and more electorates begin to perceive government officials to be elements of graft and corruption. States that ANY MEMBER OF THE BOARD OF INSPECTORS OR BOARDOF CANVASSERS OR ANY PUBLIC OFFICIAL FOUND GUILTY OF TAMPERING, INCREASING OR DECREASING VOTES RECEIVED BY CANDIDATE OR REFUSES TO CREDIT THE CORRECT VOTES, TAMPER, ALTER, MODIFY, DEDUCT SUCH VOTES SHALL BE SENTENCED TO SUFFER THE PENALTY IMPOSED AGAINST HEINOUS CRIMES as prescribed under RA 7659, the Death Penalty Law.

rows.abstract: Rationale: "... taxable income has escaped close scrutiny among tax collectors because the clients ... rarely report the professional fees involved and paid ..." States that --- "SECTION 1. A person who pays a fee of not less than One Hundred Fiftythousand Pesos (P150,000.00), whether in cash or in kind, for services rendered by another in the exercise or practice of his profession requiring government examination shall submit a report in the form to be prepared by the Secretary of Finance, tothe Commissioner of Internal Revenue or his duly authorized representative within ten (10) days after the close of each month indicating the following information and such information which the Secretary of Finance imposes: (1) Name of professionaland client; (2)  Kind of professional service rendered; (3) Inclusive date of service rendered; and (4) Date of payment and amount of professional fee received.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ADOPTING A COMPUTERIZED SYSTEM OF ELECTION FOR THE 1998 GENERAL ELECTIONS AND SUBSEQUENT ELECTIONS, PLEBISCITES, REFERENDA, RECALL AND OTHER ELECTORAL EXERCISES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF BATAS PAMBANSA BLG. 881, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE
rows.abstract: Rationale: On June 7, 1995, Congress passed into law R.A. No. 8046, authorizing the COMELEC to conduct a nationwide demonstration of a computerized election and pilot-test it in the September 9, 1996 elections in the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.  The pilot-testing serves as the preparatory exercise for a nationwide implementation of a computerized election system.  Such system is envisioned to fully modernize and improve our electoral processes and thereby minimize, if not prevent altogether, incidents of fraud and other irregularities. Provides for these areas of concern: (1) Use of the AIS-150 Optical Scanner; (2) Printing and distribution of official ballots; (3) Examination and testing of counting machineries; and (4) Electionn offenses.
rows.status: Substituted by HB09397

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 75 OF CHAPTER 1, TITLE IV OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 209, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Of the numerous and multifarious issues brough before the courts, one of the most difficult and sensitive to resolve is that involving property relations between husband andd wife. States that --- "SECTION 1. The future spouses may, in the marriage settlements, agree upon the absolute community, conjugal partnership of gains, complete separation of property, or any other regime.  In the absence of marriage settlements, or when the regime agreed upon is void, the system of CONJUGAL PARTNERSHIP OF GAINS as established in this Code shall govern."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 1996-09-23

rows.author: A103
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 96, CHAPTER 3, AND ARTICLE 124, CHAPTER 4, TITLE IV OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 209, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale:  to provide the wife an  equal standing with the husbandd insofar as the administration and enjoyment of the community property or conjugal partnership property is concerned, and to conform to the constitutional mandate and the avowed objective of the Family Code, it is imperative to amend Articles 96 and 124 of the same. Further, that recourse to the courts shall be available  to both spouses as soon as possible so that the five-year period can be shortened to a period of thirty (30) days from the date of failure of conciliation between them. Amends Article 96, Chapter 3, Title 4 of the Family Code to read as follows: "The administration and enjoyment of the community property shall belong to both spouses jointly.  In case of ddisagreement, the husband's decision shall prevail ONLY IF THE COMMUNITY PROPERTY WAS OBTAINED THROUGH HIS SOLE EFFORTS; BUT IF THE MAJOR PORTION THEREOF OR ITS VALUE IS DERIVED FROM THE WIFE'S RESOURCES AND EFFORTS, HER DECISION SHALL PREVAIL, subje

rows.abstract: "SECTION 1. rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ABOLISH THE PRESCRIPTIVE PERIOD FOR ACTIONS TO ANNUL MARRIAGES CELEBRATED BEFORE THE ENACTMENT OF THE FAMILY CODE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 39 OF THE FAMILY CODE
rows.abstract: Proposes that the PRESCRIPTIVE PERIOD provided in Article 39 of the Family Code be DELETED so that marriages solemnized BEFORE the effectivity of the Family Code MAY BE ANNULLED at any time, as long as the grounds therefor exist. Rationale: Under Article 39 of the Family Code, action or defense for the declaration of absolute nullity of a marriage shall not prescribe. However, in cases of marriages celebrated before the effectivity of the Family Code, such action or defense shall presscribe inten years after the Code shall have taken effect. > The reason given for the exception was that couples who were married before the effectivity of the Family Code who have grounds for annulment by reason of psychological incapacity, but who do not avvail off the 10 year prescriptive period provided under Article 39 of the Family code show no interest in annulling their marriage.
